messages:
Anya Patel: quick a11y pass on the Models table — VoiceOver (mac/ios) seems to drop keyboard focus when you open the row action menu. Can repro reliably. Screenshot attached.
Maya Chen: can you drop steps? which row action — the kebab or the inline buttons?
Anya Patel: steps: tab to table -> use arrow keys to move rows -> press Enter on a row to open details -> press Tab to get to kebab (...) -> press Enter to open menu -> VoiceOver focus jumps to top of page instead of the menu.
Chris O'Neill: that sounds like a focus trap escape when we set display:none on something. Any console errors?
Anya Patel: no console errors. Happens both with VoiceOver rotor and keyboard only. Happens on latest Safari+macOS.
Samir Gupta: can repro on Chrome + NVDA too, but NVDA focuses the body not top of page. Likely we remove the menu from DOM briefly then reinsert which resets the active element.
Priya Rao: is the menu rendered via portal? I vaguely remember we reparent menus into #modals for z-index. Portals can shift focus if we don't preserve the activeElement.
a11y-bot: automated-check: color-contrast for .table-row--hover-bg against body background = 2.9:1 (fails AA for large text), focus outline width < 3px flagged.
Maya Chen: two separate issues then: focus persistence and contrast of hover state. Let's tackle focus first. If it's a portal reparent, solution is to manage focus programmatically: on menu open call menuEl.focus() and set aria-expanded on the trigger.
Chris O'Neill: agree. Also prefer using role="menu" and role="menuitem" semantics, plus add aria-controls to the trigger so screen readers can announce relationship.
Samir Gupta: quick patch idea — when opening menu we avoid removing the trigger from DOM. Instead, keep trigger node and toggle visibility with aria-hidden. Also ensure we call preventScroll when focusing to avoid jumping: element.focus({preventScroll: true}).
Anya Patel: small nuance — using preventScroll stops voiceover from moving the viewport, but VO still sometimes announces wrong place if the DOM order changes. So prefer focusing the actual menu node after portal mount sync.
Priya Rao: accessibility nit: the open menu should set aria-expanded="true" on the trigger button and the menu should have aria-labelledby referencing the trigger id. Also add aria-live="polite" region for error messages only, not for menu open.
Maya Chen: can someone draft a small code snippet we can try?
Chris O'Neill: here's a proposed snippet — feel free to copy it into the components repo:
```
// openMenu.ts
function openMenu(triggerEl, menuEl) {
  // render menu in portal first, then focus
  requestAnimationFrame(() => {
    menuEl.setAttribute('role','menu')
    menuEl.setAttribute('aria-labelledby', triggerEl.id)
    triggerEl.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true')
    menuEl.focus({preventScroll: true})
  })
}
```

Samir Gupta: also add a tabindex="-1" on the menu container so it can receive programmatic focus. And use :focus-visible for showing the ring instead of always-on outline.
Anya Patel: thanks. For contrast — a11y-bot flagged hover bg. Current token is --bg-hover-weak which is only 2.9:1. We need >= 3:1 for large text or 4.5 for normal. Table rows text is 14px normal, so should be 4.5:1.
Priya Rao: suggestion: use --bg-hover-strong token (darker) or add a subtle border to indicate hover instead of changing background color. Border approach helps maintain text contrast.
Maya Chen: can we test swapping to --bg-hover-strong in storybook and run axe? If it passes, we'll adopt.
Samir Gupta: created a quick CSS diff to try:
```
.table-row:hover {
  background: var(--bg-hover-strong);
}
.table-row:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid var(--focus-accent);
  outline-offset: 2px;
}
.menu-container[role="menu"] { tabindex: -1 }
```

Chris O'Neill: tiny correction — tabindex should be attribute not CSS. But idea is clear. Also ensure focus ring color meets contrast ratio against background. Use color-contrast-tools to pick token.
Anya Patel: UX question — when a row expands (details accordion), VoiceOver reads the whole content. Should we move focus into the expanded region or leave it on the trigger?
Priya Rao: generally move focus to the expanded panel only if the expansion is a modal-like change or user initiates an action that needs next step. For inline details, keep focus on trigger but provide aria-expanded and make sure panel has role="region" and aria-labelledby so screen reader can find it.
Maya Chen: agreed. We'll keep focus on the trigger for keyboard users. But add a short sr-only hint inside the panel: "Press Tab to navigate panel actions" so user knows there are interactive items.
Samir Gupta: I'll open a draft PR with the focus handling + CSS token swap. Attaching steps + repro in the PR description.
Anya Patel: thanks Samir. Can you also add a tiny test in cypress that tabs into the menu and asserts document.activeElement is the menu after open? That will prevent regressions.
Samir Gupta: yep will add cypress test.
Chris O'Neill: leaving a note — update the component Storybook stories with VoiceOver checklist and run axe.
Maya Chen: thanks all. Assigning to @Samir for the fix. Will follow up after PR review. :thumbsup:
Samir Gupta: sounds good — starting work now, will ping when draft PR is up. :rocket:
